title: Index Funds & Ethereum: My Investment Strategy Revealed
description: Discover how a capital allocation strategy mirroring top investors, focusing on index funds and a long-term Ethereum holding, can be highly beneficial. Learn from insights into blockchain development. #IndexFunds #InvestingStrategy #Ethereum #CapitalAllocation #Blockchain

asr.full_text: Why index funds? You're the reason I- your capital allocation strategy is almost identical to mine. I want to talk about the house thing as well, but after reading your book, I stopped trying to pick stocks. Yeah. And I invested all of my available capital into index funds, outside of investing in starting companies. So I'm a shareholder in I don't know, 50, 60, 70 companies. I, all my other available capital is invested in the index funds. And then I have a very long standing, large position in Ethereum, which I've held for like six years or something, which has done me very well. Yeah. That is it. And the Ethereum investment is also based on the fact that I run a software business that is in blockchain. And I could see that developers are building on top of Ethereum more than any other blockchain. So that insight was really beneficial to me. And six years. So even with the big fall over the last two years, you're still up a lot.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents an interview-style discussion of one speaker’s personal approach to index funds, startup investments, and Ethereum rather than a concrete offer directed at viewers. The Ethereum segment reports that the speaker’s long-held position performed well, but does not establish a promised or guaranteed future return, required payment, or requested audience action. The financial content is therefore contextualized as personal investment commentary.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary subject is investment commentary: the speaker discusses allocating capital to index funds and startups, holding Ethereum, and the available video evidence and reported past performance of that holding. The supplied evidence does not show a concrete offer, payment requirement, or guaranteed future return.
